evidenceClaims.claim: 用途：Tiny 200b functional Event Emitter / pubsub（微型功能性事件发射器/发布订阅系统）
类型：支持 IE9+ 的浏览器原生事件发射器，无依赖，支持 Node 及模块打包器

主要模块职责：mitt 工厂函数创建 Emitter 实例，all 属性存储事件处理器列表，on/off/emit 方法实现注册/注销/触发逻辑

explorer.projectSummary: Mitt is a lightweight (~200b gzipped) functional event emitter library written in TypeScript. It provides an Event Emitter/PubSub interface with support for wildcard events ('*'), designed for browsers and Node.js environments without external dependencies. The core logic is implemented in src/index.ts, which exports type definitions and the main mitt factory function. The package.json defines the build configuration and entry points.

evidenceClaims.claim: 核心实现：`mitt` 函数接收可选的 `EventHandlerMap` 作为初始化参数，内部维护一个 `Map` 存储事件类型到处理器的映射，通过 `on`/`off`/`emit` 方法操作该 Map。
静态依赖：无外部运行时依赖，依赖 TypeScript 类型系统（泛型 `Events`、`Handler`、`WildcardHandler`）和原生 `Map` API。
架构：纯函数式工厂模式，返回一个包含 `all`（内部 Map）、`on`（注册）、`off`（注销）、`emit`（触发）属性的对象。

mentor.architectureOverview: Mitt 是一个基于 TypeScript 泛型的轻量级事件发射器。核心逻辑位于 `src/index.ts`，通过 `mitt` 工厂函数实例化。它利用原生 `Map` 存储事件处理器列表，支持普通事件类型和通配符 `'*'`。类型系统定义了 `Handler`、`WildcardHandler` 和 `EventHandlerMap` 以提供类型安全。

readingPath.why: 查看类型定义（L1-L21）和工厂函数实现（L46-L94），理解 `on`/`off`/`emit` 的逻辑。
验证 `on` 方法注册逻辑（L56-L77）、`off` 方法注销逻辑（L82-L90）以及 `emit` 方法触发逻辑（L19-L21）。

keyPatterns.description: 使用 `Map.get` 获取处理器列表，`push` 添加，`splice` 移除特定处理器，或清空列表。
当类型为 `'*'` 时，使用 `WildcardHandler` 类型，逻辑与普通事件类似但类型约束不同。

# Mitt > Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub. - **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped - **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events - **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter) - **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this` - **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples & Demos](#examples--demos) - [API](#api) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [License](#license) ## Install This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html ``` You can find the library on `window.mitt`. ## Usage ```js import mitt from 'mitt' const emitter = mitt() // listen to an event emitter.on('foo', e => console.log('foo', e) ) // listen to all events emitter.on('*', (type, e) => console.log(type, e) ) // fire an event emitter.emit('foo', { a: 'b' }) // clearing all events emitter.all.clear() // working with handler references: function onFoo() {} emitter.on('foo', onFoo) // listen emitter.off('foo', onFoo) // unlisten ``` ### Typescript Set `"strict": true` in your tsconfig.json to get improved type inference for `mitt` instance methods. ```ts import mitt from 'mitt'; type Events = { foo: string; bar?: number; }; const emitter = mitt(); // inferred as Emitter emitter.on('foo', (e) => {}); // 'e' has inferred type 'string' emitter.emit('foo', 42); // Error: Argument of type 'number' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'. Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html ``` You can find the library on `window.mitt`. ## Usage ```js import mitt from 'mitt' const emitter = mitt() // listen to an event emitter.on('foo', e => console.log('foo', e) ) // listen to all events emitter.on('*', (type, e) => console.log(type, e) ) // fire an event emitter.emit('foo', { a: 'b' }) // clearing all events emitter.all.clear() // working with handler references: function onFoo() {} emitter.on('foo', onFoo) // listen emitter.off('foo', onFoo) // unlisten ``` ### Typescript Set `"strict": true` in your tsconfig.json to get improved type inference for `mitt` instance methods. ```ts import mitt from 'mitt'; type Events = { foo: string; bar?: number; }; const emitter = mitt(); // inferred as Emitter emitter.on('foo', (e) => {}); // 'e' has inferred type 'string' emitter.emit('foo', 42); // Error: Argument of type 'number' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'. (2345) ``` Alternatively, you can use the provided `Emitter` type:

# Mitt > Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub. - **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped - **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events - **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter) - **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this` - **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples & Demos](#examples--demos) - [API](#api) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [License](#license) ## Install This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html ``` You can find the library on `window.mitt`. ## Usage ```js import mitt from 'mitt' const emitter = mitt() // listen to an event emitter.on('foo', e => console.log('foo', e) ) // listen to all events emitter.on('*', (type, e) => console.log(type, e) ) // fire an event emitter.emit('foo', { a: 'b' }) // clearing all events emitter.all.clear() // working with handler references: function onFoo() {} emitter.on('foo', onFoo) // listen emitter.off('foo', onFoo) // unlisten ``` ### Typescript Set `"strict": true` in your tsconfig.json to get improved type inference for `mitt` instance methods. ```ts import mitt from 'mitt'; type Events = { foo: string; bar?: number; }; const emitter = mitt(); // inferred as Emitter emitter.on('foo', (e) => {}); // 'e' has inferred type 'string' emitter.emit('foo', 42); // Error: Argument of type 'number' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'. evidenceClaims.claim: 核心实现：`mitt` 函数接收可选的 `EventHandlerMap` 作为初始化参数，内部维护一个 `Map` 存储事件类型到处理器的映射，通过 `on`/`off`/`emit` 方法操作该 Map。
静态依赖：无外部运行时依赖，依赖 TypeScript 类型系统（泛型 `Events`、`Handler`、`WildcardHandler`）和原生 `Map` API。
架构：纯函数式工厂模式，返回一个包含 `all`（内部 Map）、`on`（注册）、`off`（注销）、`emit`（触发）属性的对象。

answer.architectureOverview: Mitt 是一个基于 TypeScript 泛型的轻量级事件发射器。核心逻辑位于 `src/index.ts`，通过 `mitt` 工厂函数实例化。它利用原生 `Map` 存储事件处理器列表，支持普通事件类型和通配符 `'*'`。类型系统定义了 `Handler`、`WildcardHandler` 和 `EventHandlerMap` 以提供类型安全。

readingPath.why: 查看类型定义（L1-L21）和工厂函数实现（L46-L94），理解 `on`/`off`/`emit` 的逻辑。
验证 `on` 方法注册逻辑（L56-L77）、`off` 方法注销逻辑（L82-L90）以及 `emit` 方法触发逻辑（L19-L21）。

keyPatterns.description: 使用 `Map.get` 获取处理器列表，`push` 添加，`splice` 移除特定处理器，或清空列表。
当类型为 `'*'` 时，使用 `WildcardHandler` 类型，逻辑与普通事件类似但类型约束不同。

function.name: read_code

function.name: trace_dependencies
function.description: Resolve static local imports of one source path. Returns related paths, not a runtime call graph. External/dynamic imports may be unresolved; read returned paths before making claims.

function.name: find_tests
function.description: Find candidate tests for a source path, optionally with a symbol query. Returns short excerpts; read relevant test ranges to verify assertions. A match does not prove executed coverage.

function.name: search_code
function.description: Search source/tests; returns at most 3 source units, bounded by bytes. Use English identifiers; match=literal for an exact substring. Empty results: change query. Optional path is exact; path_prefix limits to a directory BEFORE retrieval. Truncated hits include next_line; read remaining relevant lines with read_code.

function.name: search_docs
function.description: Search README/docs/config (not source). Same bounded locations/excerpts as search_code. Use English keywords; path/path_prefix filter BEFORE retrieval; empty results do not prove absence.

function.name: read_code
function.description: Read exact source or documentation lines from the snapshot. Supply path, start_line, end_line. Optional expand=symbol includes the enclosing function/class/test. At most 100 lines, bounded bytes; next_line means more remains. Only shown lines can be cited.

function.name: trace_dependencies
function.description: Resolve static local imports of one source path. Returns related paths, not a runtime call graph. External/dynamic imports may be unresolved; read returned paths before making claims.

function.name: find_tests
function.description: Find candidate tests for a source path, optionally with a symbol query. Returns short excerpts; read relevant test ranges to verify assertions. A match does not prove executed coverage.

context.content: # Mitt > Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub. - **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped - **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events - **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter) - **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this` - **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples & Demos](#examples--demos) - [API](#api) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [License](#license) ## Install This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html

{
  "name": "mitt",
  "version": "3.0.1",
  "description": "Tiny 200b functional Event Emitter / pubsub.",
  "module": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "main": "dist/mitt.js",
  "jsnext:main": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "umd:main": "dist/mitt.umd.js",
  "source": "src/index.ts",
  "typings": "index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "types": "./index.d.ts",
    "module": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/mitt.js",
    "default": "./dist/mitt.mjs"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "npm-run-all --silent typecheck lint mocha test-types",
    "mocha": "mocha test",
    "test-types": "tsc test/test-types-compilation.ts --noEmit --strict",
    "lint": "eslint src test --ext ts --ext js",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "bundle": "microbundle -f es,cjs,umd",
    "build": "npm-run-all --silent clean -p bundle -s docs",
    "clean": "rimraf dist",
    "docs": "documentation readme src/index.ts --section API -q --parse-extension ts",
    "release": "npm run -s build -s && npm t && git commit -am $npm_package_version && git tag $npm_package_version && git push && git push --tags && npm publish"
  },
  "repository": "developit/mitt",

function.name: search_docs

function.name: read_code

function.name: trace_dependencies
function.description: Resolve static local imports of one source path. Returns related paths, not a runtime call graph. External/dynamic imports may be unresolved; read returned paths before making claims.

function.name: find_tests
function.description: Find candidate tests for a source path, optionally with a symbol query. Returns short excerpts; read relevant test ranges to verify assertions. A match does not prove executed coverage.

function.name: search_docs

function.name: read_code
function.description: Read exact source or documentation lines from the snapshot. Supply path, start_line, end_line. Optional expand=symbol includes the enclosing function/class/test. At most 100 lines, bounded bytes; next_line means more remains. Only shown lines can be cited.

function.name: trace_dependencies
function.description: Resolve static local imports of one source path. Returns related paths, not a runtime call graph. External/dynamic imports may be unresolved; read returned paths before making claims.

function.name: find_tests
function.description: Find candidate tests for a source path, optionally with a symbol query. Returns short excerpts; read relevant test ranges to verify assertions. A match does not prove executed coverage.

source_spans.content: # Mitt > Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub. - **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped - **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events - **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter) - **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this` - **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples & Demos](#examples--demos) - [API](#api) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [License](#license) ## Install This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html

{
  "name": "mitt",
  "version": "3.0.1",
  "description": "Tiny 200b functional Event Emitter / pubsub.",
  "module": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "main": "dist/mitt.js",
  "jsnext:main": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "umd:main": "dist/mitt.umd.js",
  "source": "src/index.ts",
  "typings": "index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "types": "./index.d.ts",
    "module": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/mitt.js",
    "default": "./dist/mitt.mjs"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "npm-run-all --silent typecheck lint mocha test-types",
    "mocha": "mocha test",
    "test-types": "tsc test/test-types-compilation.ts --noEmit --strict",
    "lint": "eslint src test --ext ts --ext js",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "bundle": "microbundle -f es,cjs,umd",
    "build": "npm-run-all --silent clean -p bundle -s docs",
    "clean": "rimraf dist",
    "docs": "documentation readme src/index.ts --section API -q --parse-extension ts",
    "release": "npm run -s build -s && npm t && git commit -am $npm_package_version && git tag $npm_package_version && git push && git push --tags && npm publish"
  },
  "repository": "developit/mitt",

source_spans.content: # Mitt > Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub. - **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped - **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events - **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter) - **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this` - **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples & Demos](#examples--demos) - [API](#api) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [License](#license) ## Install This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html

{
  "name": "mitt",
  "version": "3.0.1",
  "description": "Tiny 200b functional Event Emitter / pubsub.",
  "module": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "main": "dist/mitt.js",
  "jsnext:main": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "umd:main": "dist/mitt.umd.js",
  "source": "src/index.ts",
  "typings": "index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "types": "./index.d.ts",
    "module": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/mitt.js",
    "default": "./dist/mitt.mjs"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "npm-run-all --silent typecheck lint mocha test-types",
    "mocha": "mocha test",
    "test-types": "tsc test/test-types-compilation.ts --noEmit --strict",
    "lint": "eslint src test --ext ts --ext js",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "bundle": "microbundle -f es,cjs,umd",
    "build": "npm-run-all --silent clean -p bundle -s docs",
    "clean": "rimraf dist",
    "docs": "documentation readme src/index.ts --section API -q --parse-extension ts",
    "release": "npm run -s build -s && npm t && git commit -am $npm_package_version && git tag $npm_package_version && git push && git push --tags && npm publish"
  },
  "repository": "developit/mitt",

context.content: # Mitt > Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub. - **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped - **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events - **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter) - **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this` - **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Examples & Demos](#examples--demos) - [API](#api) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [License](#license) ## Install This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed. ```sh $ npm install --save mitt ``` Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else: ```javascript // using ES6 modules import mitt from 'mitt' // using CommonJS modules var mitt = require('mitt') ``` The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com): ```html

{
  "name": "mitt",
  "version": "3.0.1",
  "description": "Tiny 200b functional Event Emitter / pubsub.",
  "module": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "main": "dist/mitt.js",
  "jsnext:main": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "umd:main": "dist/mitt.umd.js",
  "source": "src/index.ts",
  "typings": "index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "types": "./index.d.ts",
    "module": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/mitt.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/mitt.js",
    "default": "./dist/mitt.mjs"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "npm-run-all --silent typecheck lint mocha test-types",
    "mocha": "mocha test",
    "test-types": "tsc test/test-types-compilation.ts --noEmit --strict",
    "lint": "eslint src test --ext ts --ext js",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "bundle": "microbundle -f es,cjs,umd",
    "build": "npm-run-all --silent clean -p bundle -s docs",
    "clean": "rimraf dist",
    "docs": "documentation readme src/index.ts --section API -q --parse-extension ts",
    "release": "npm run -s build -s && npm t && git commit -am $npm_package_version && git tag $npm_package_version && git push && git push --tags && npm publish"
  },
  "repository": "developit/mitt",
